title: fix(video-editor): preserve clip speed preview position
body:
## What changed
- remapped preview playback position when clip timelines change so speed edits keep the preview on the same source frame instead of reusing a stale global position
- centralized clip speed range calculation and used it both for bloc normalization and the speed sheet slider bounds
- cleaned up clip-speed history writes to use fresh bloc state and the shared `setClipState(...)` helper
- added targeted speed telemetry for normalized speed changes and preview remaps
- added regression tests for speed range calculation, preview remapping, and speed sheet bounds

## Why
Changing a clip's speed rebuilt the preview composition with the old playback position. When the new composition became shorter, the preview could seek at or past the new end and loop immediately, which looked like the editor was always previewing the fastest speed.

The UI also exposed speeds that the bloc would later clamp silently, and the speed flow was writing history from a stale pre-sheet clip snapshot.

## Impact
- speed previews now stay on the expected frame after a speed change
- the speed slider only offers valid values for the current composition constraints
- future log exports will show requested/applied speed changes and preview remaps for this path

## Validation
- `flutter test test/widgets/video_editor/timeline_editor/controls/video_editor_clip_speed_sheet_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/widgets/video_editor/main_editor/video_editor_canvas_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/blocs/video_editor/clip_editor/clip_editor_bloc_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/blocs/video_editor test/widgets/video_editor`
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test`

Closes #4689.

title: fix(video-editor): speed preview seeks to wrong position after clip speed change
body:
## Summary
Adjusting a clip's playback speed in the video editor can restart preview playback at the wrong position.

## Symptoms
- after changing speed, preview can appear to jump to the end and loop immediately
- this can make the editor look like it is always previewing the fastest speed regardless of the selected value
- exported logs have not been sufficient to diagnose which speed was requested or applied

## Root cause
The editor rebuilt the preview composition after a speed change but reused the old global playback position. When the new composition became shorter, that stale position could land at or beyond the new end. The speed UI also exposed values that were later silently clamped by editor constraints.

## Desired behavior
- preserve the same source frame when the clip timeline is rebuilt after a speed change
- clamp safely when an exact remap is not possible
- show only valid speed values in the editor UI
- emit logs that capture requested speed, applied speed, and preview remap behavior

## Tracking
Fixed by PR #4688.

title: revert(security): restore custodial BYOK secure-account upgrade
body:
Closes #4676

  Revert PR #4665 because it disables the intended secure-account / BYOK functionality rather than fixing the actual issue.

  The secure-account flow is meant to transfer the user’s local `nsec` to Keycast for custodial backup / managed signing while preserving the same Nostr identity. Removing that
  path entirely is a product regression, not a security fix.

  The real bug is narrower: the `nsec` was also being embedded in PKCE verifier material and could propagate through pending verification, token exchange, logs, and OAuth plumbing.
  That should be fixed surgically by keeping PKCE random-only and hardening the explicit Keycast import path.

  Follow-up: divinevideo/keycast#242 tracks encrypting custodial BYOK import to a Keycast KMS asymmetric public key so generic HTTP infrastructure sees ciphertext rather than raw
  `nsec`.

## Description

This PR replaces the old MediaKit video-player with the new DivineVideoPlayer which uses native-video-player apis.

title: fix(security): strip BYOK nsec from Keycast OAuth and gate secure-account upgrade
body:
## Description

**Phase 1 (mobile emergency block) for the BYOK `nsec` leak.** The secure-account upgrade exported the user's local `nsec` (Nostr private key) and sent it to Keycast over the wire — in the `POST /api/headless/register` body as `body['nsec']`, and embedded in the PKCE `code_verifier` as a `<random>.<nsec1…>` suffix (which is then hashed into the OAuth `code_challenge`), plus a derived `byok_pubkey` query param. The private key left on-device custody.

This PR removes that surface entirely and **gates** the upgrade behind a notice rather than falling through to the server's auto-generate path — which would silently re-create the user's identity under a new server-managed pubkey and wipe their local social-graph caches (via `shouldClearDataForUser`). That destructive auto-generate behavior is what closed the prior attempt (#3784); gating avoids it. Identity preservation is restored separately by #3786 via the proof-of-possession contract (divinevideo/keycast#197).

> **Draft on purpose.** #3359 is the home of an unresolved product decision (custodial-secure key transport vs. local-only proof-of-possession). This PR implements the *decision-independent* interim: stop the live key leak now, without the destructive regression that closed #3784. It does **not** pre-commit the durable direction.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #3359 · Follow-up: #3786 · Server contract: divinevideo/keycast#197

## Reproducing the leak (before this PR)

1. Launch the app as a fresh anonymous user (auto-generated local key).
2. Go to **Settings → Secure Your Account** (or tap the profile "Secure your account" prompt). Enter an email + password and submit.
3. Inspect the outbound `POST /api/headless/register` body → it contains `"nsec": "nsec1…"` — the user's private key.
4. Inspect the subsequent `POST /api/oauth/token` body → `code_verifier` is `<random>.nsec1…`; the same nsec is therefore also hashed into the `code_challenge` on the authorize URL and persisted in `pending_verification` secure storage.

→ The private key has left the device in plaintext over the network and is embedded in the OAuth challenge. (Audit evidence: `pkce.dart:9-12`, `oauth_client.dart:155-171/280-310`, `secure_account_screen.dart:100-141`.)

## Verifying the fix

- `nsec` / `byok_pubkey` no longer exist on the `keycast_flutter` OAuth API, so no caller can send them.
- The secure-account entry points are hidden; the screen shows a paused notice and makes **no** registration request.
- `bash mobile/tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` passes, and a new `nsec-leak-guard` CI job fails any future reintroduction of `body['nsec']` / `'nsec':`.
- Negative-regression tests assert the nsec never appears in the verifier, request body, or persisted state.

## What changed

**Client (`keycast_flutter`)**
- `pkce.dart` — `generateVerifier()` drops the `nsec` param; always returns pure-random base64url.
- `oauth_client.dart` — removed `nsec`/`byokPubkey` from `getAuthorizationUrl` and `headlessRegister`, the `body['nsec']` field, the `byok_pubkey` query param, and the now-orphaned `KeyUtils` import.

**App**
- `pending_verification_service.dart` — `load()` purges any persisted `*nsec1*` verifier (from pre-fix devices) before it can be replayed to the token endpoint.
- `email_verification_cubit.dart` — stops logging the verifier value (presence booleans only).
- `secure_account_screen.dart` — gutted to an l10n notice (no form / no `exportNsec` / no registration).
- `settings_screen.dart` + `profile_action_type.dart` — both entry points hidden, each with a `// TODO(#3786):` restore marker.
- New `authSecureAccountUnavailableMessage` l10n key (registered in `arb_consistency_test` untranslated-debt; non-English falls back to English until the next pass).

**CI**
- `tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` + a `nsec-leak-guard` job wired into the `mobile-ci` aggregate gate.

## Out of Scope

- **Restoring BYOK identity preservation** — #3786 (proof-of-possession), gated on divinevideo/keycast#197 reaching production. Until then the upgrade is paused; anonymous users cannot upgrade / back up their key.
- **Already-exfiltrated keys** captured in infra/proxy logs pre-fix — retention review tracked in keycast#197; whether to prompt affected users to rotate keys is a separate product/security decision.
- The durable architecture decision (custodial-secure vs. local-only) — needs product sign-off here / on #3359.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` → No issues found; `keycast_flutter` analyze → clean
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` (15 changed files) → clean
- `keycast_flutter`: 78 tests pass (`pkce_test`, `oauth_client_test`)
- App tests pass: `pending_verification_service_test` (new, 4), `secure_account_screen_test`, `profile_action_type_test`, `settings_screen_test`, `email_verification_cubit_test`, `arb_consistency_test`
- `bash mobile/tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` → passes
- `integration_test/auth/session_expired_banner_test.dart` is **skipped** pending #3786 — it relies on the BYOK local-key fallback this PR removes (the expired-session banner only appears because the local key shares the OAuth pubkey), so it cannot run meaningfully until identity preservation is restored.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Build configuration change

> Reviewer note: this intentionally **pauses** the secure-account upgrade UX until #3786. Existing secured users are unaffected; only new anonymous→secured upgrades are paused. Please weigh the interim UX gap against keeping the live private-key leak open.

title: fix(invite): guard invite status lifecycle and auth gating
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4393.

This hardens `InviteStatusCubit` against the two failure modes currently showing up around invite-status loads:
- async completion after the cubit has already been closed
- expected cold-start auth gaps that briefly make invite requests unauthenticated and return `401 auth_required`

## Root cause

`InviteStatusCubit.load()` and `generateInvite()` emitted state unconditionally after awaited network work completed. If the settings surface or app shell disposed the cubit first, Bloc would raise an `emit after close` error.

Separately, invite-status loads could run before NIP-98 auth was ready to mint headers on cold start or resume. That produced a transient `401` from the invite service, which the cubit treated as a generic failure even though the underlying app session had not actually failed.

## What changed

- Added an `isInviteAuthReady` gate to `InviteStatusCubit` and wired it from `nip98AuthServiceProvider.canCreateTokens` in `main.dart`.
- Prevented invite-status requests from starting while invite auth is not ready.
- Restored the previous invite state instead of surfacing a generic error when the invite API returns the expected `401 auth_required` gap.
- Added `_emitIfOpen(...)` so late async completions do not emit after the cubit has been closed.
- Added focused tests for:
  - auth-not-ready no-op behavior
  - `401 auth_required` rollback to previous state
  - close-before-completion lifecycle safety

## Why this is safe

- The change is local to the invite cubit boundary and its provider wiring.
- Successful invite fetch and invite generation paths are unchanged.
- Unexpected failures still flow through `addError(...)` and the existing error state.
- The new auth gate only blocks invite calls when the app cannot currently create the required NIP-98 header.

## Validation

Local:
- `flutter test test/blocs/invite_status/invite_status_cubit_test.dart`
- `flutter analyze lib/blocs/invite_status/invite_status_cubit.dart lib/main.dart test/blocs/invite_status/invite_status_cubit_test.dart`
- pre-push repo gate: changed-file analyze + changed-file tests

Notes:
- A full `flutter analyze` in this checkout still reports the repo's pre-existing `avoid_print` infos in `integration_test_manual/`, `scripts/`, and `tools/`. The touched invite files are clean.

the same NIP-17 seal + gift-wrap envelope as the underlying DM (NIP-17
spec line 14 explicitly allows kind-7 reactions inside the encrypted
chat), so privacy is reuse-of-spec rather than custom design.

- 6-emoji quick row + `+` entry, shown above the existing Copy / Delete
  / Report actions in a single long-press overlay.
- Compact bordered chip beneath the bubble, overlapping its bottom
  corner. Own / theirs / pending / failed variants.
- Cap one reaction per user per message in v1; supersede on a
  different emoji emits NIP-09 kind-5 deletion of the prior.
- Hidden on failed-send own DMs.

## Architecture

UI → BLoC → Repository → Client, per `architecture.md`.

| Layer | Files |
|---|---|
| Client | None — reuses `NIP17MessageService.buildRumor(eventKind: 7)` + `sendRumor` unchanged. |
| Repository | `dm_repository` extended with `DmReactionsRepository` + reportable-sites constants; new branch at `_handleGiftWrapEvent` line 511 routes `rumor.kind == 7` to the new repo before the existing 14/15 gate. |
| BLoC | `lib/blocs/dm/reactions/` — cubit with restartable/sequential transformers and addError-without-Reportable per the matrix. |
| Persistence | `DmMessageReactions` Drift table (dedup on `(id, owner_pubkey)`, partial indexes, soft-delete + rumor JSON columns) + `DmReactionsDao` (insertOptimistic / swapPlaceholderId / markPending / markFailed / softDelete / upsertIncoming / watchForConversation). |
| Widgets | `ReactionChip` in `divine_ui` (strict-coverage tests included); `ReactionsRow` + `ReactionPickerOverlay` in the feature folder. |
| l10n | 11 new `dmReaction*` keys in `app_en.arb`, added to `_knownUntranslatedDebt` (matches #4631 markdown precedent). |

## Reliability hardening

The user reproduced a retry-doesn't-work scenario: a failed reaction
could not be retried by tapping, but a single retry tap after
hot-restart succeeded. Three compounding bugs caused it:

1. **No timeout on `sendRumor`** — a stalled relay socket left the
   awaited future hanging indefinitely; the `sequential()` event
   transformer queued every subsequent retry behind the hung one.
   **Fix:** wrap `sendRumor` in a 15 s timeout
   (`_sendRumorWithTimeout` in the repository, applied to both
   `publish` and `retry`). Timeouts surface as `NIP17SendFailure`.
2. **No DAO-persisted in-flight state** — the cubit's in-memory
   `pending` map was the only signal of a retry in progress; a cubit
   rebuild (auth flip, navigation, hot-restart) lost it and the chip
   reverted to the stale persisted state. **Fix:** new
   `DmReactionsDao.markPending` writes `publishStatus = 'pending'`
   to the row before the send. On any non-success outcome (timeout,
   failure, throw) the row flips back to `'failed'`, so the chip is
   tappable again immediately.
3. **`BlocSelector` missed pending-map updates** — the row selector
   was keyed only on `state.reactionsFor(messageId)`, so transitions
   in `state.pending` did not rebuild the chip and the captured
   `agg.isFailed` could be stale. **Fix:** swap to `BlocBuilder`
   with a per-message `buildWhen` that includes both the reactions
   list and this message's pending entries. Also added a guard at
   the top of `_onTap` to drop taps on pending chips so a tap during
   retry can't fall through to the toggle branch and silently delete
   the in-flight reaction.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean (32.5s).
- [x] `divine_ui` package tests: 585 / 585 (includes 9 new chip tests).
- [x] `dm_repository` package tests: 240 / 240 (no regression from the
      kind-7 routing branch + new constructor parameter).
- [x] `db_client` package tests: 616 / 616 (the new table is additive).
- [x] `ConversationView` widget tests: 33 / 33 (the existing pump
      helper now provides a mock `ConversationReactionsCubit`).
- [x] `ConversationReactionsCubit` blocTest cases: 4 / 4.
- [x] `arb_consistency_test.dart` passes with the 11 new keys added
      to `_knownUntranslatedDebt`.

### Manual reproduction of the retry hardening

1. Send a DM to a peer.
2. Disconnect the device from the network OR force-stop the configured
   DM relays so the next publish hangs.
3. Long-press your sent bubble → tap any emoji from the quick row.
4. **Before this PR:** chip flips to failed; tapping it does nothing
   until the app is hot-restarted.
5. **After this PR:** chip flips to pending while the send is
   in-flight; within ≤ 15 s it falls back to failed; tapping it again
   actually re-attempts; multiple rapid taps are dropped while pending
   so the optimistic state cannot be silently destroyed.

### Manual reproduction of the happy path

1. Open a DM conversation.
2. Long-press any bubble → quick-row picker overlays the action sheet.
3. Tap ❤️ → chip appears on the bubble's bottom corner immediately
   (optimistic), persists across app restart, and lands on the peer
   via the existing NIP-17 pipeline.
4. Long-press the same bubble → tap a different emoji → the prior
   chip disappears (cap-at-one supersede via kind-5 deletion) and
   the new one appears.

## Out of scope for v1

Tracked separately as follow-up issues:

- Full `emoji_picker_flutter` wiring for the `+` entry.
- Group-DM reaction routing (1:1 only at v1).
- Reaction notifications (encrypted variant — needs its own privacy spec).
- Multi-react per message (drop the cap-at-one).
- Full ARB translation for the 16 non-English locales.
- Reaction detail sheet (only useful once groups land).

## Notes

- Brainstorm doc covering the 60-round design exploration lives
  locally at
  `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-23-issue4633-dm-emoji-reactions-brainstorm.md`
  and is intentionally not committed.
- Draft because (a) optional design check on the quick-row emoji set
  ❤️ 😂 🔥 😮 😢 👍 before merge, and (b) manual repro of the retry
  hardening on a real device is recommended before flipping to ready.

type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Summary

Let users react to a DM message with an emoji, the way they can in iMessage, WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram, and Discord. Today there is no react affordance on a DM bubble — the long-press sheet on `message_actions_sheet.dart` only exposes Copy / Copy video URL / Delete / Report. Users coming from any other messenger find the absence jarring.

## How would this be useful?

Reactions are the lowest-friction way to acknowledge a message — a thumbs up on a plan, a heart on a photo, a laugh on a joke. Without them, the only way to respond is to type a reply, which is heavier and clutters the thread.

## Proposed scope (initial)

- Long-press on any DM bubble → quick reaction row (5–6 default emojis, e.g. ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🙏 🫶 — final set TBD with design) plus a "+" entry into a full picker.
- Tapping a reaction toggles it (tap again to un-react). One reaction per user per message at first; multi-react can land later.
- Reactions render as a small chip beneath the bubble showing emoji + count, with own reactions highlighted.
- Tapping the chip shows who reacted with what (1:1 DM means just the other party, but the affordance should work for future group DMs).
- Sent and received bubbles behave identically.

Out of scope for the first pass:
- Custom / animated reactions
- Reaction notifications (separate decision — see Notes)
- Group DM reactions (no group DMs yet)

## Privacy considerations

This is the interesting part — we are trying to maximize privacy within the constraints of what we have.

We already ship NIP-25 reactions (kind 7) for videos and comments via `mobile/packages/likes_repository/`. **Reusing that primitive verbatim for DMs would leak metadata**: a plaintext kind-7 event tagged with the encrypted DM's id would publicly announce "user A reacted to event B" even though B is a NIP-17 gift-wrapped DM that should not be linkable to either party.

The reaction must be wrapped the same way the underlying DM is:

- DM messages are kind 14 (chat message) sealed (kind 13) and gift-wrapped (kind 1059) per NIP-17.
- A reaction needs the same envelope: a kind-7 (or DM-scoped reaction kind — open question) sealed and gift-wrapped to the recipient(s). The outer 1059 must not reveal which message is being reacted to.
- The inner reaction event references the DM's id via an `e` tag, which is only visible after unwrap.
- Both participants need a copy (sender wraps to self + recipient, mirroring how outgoing DMs are stored — see `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation/` and `mobile/packages/dm_repository/`).

Open spec questions to resolve before implementation:
- [ ] Reuse kind 7 inside the seal, or define a DM-specific reaction kind? (Reuse keeps interop with other NIP-17 clients that might already do this; a new kind avoids ambiguity.)
- [ ] How does the recipient enumerate reactions for a given DM? The seal carries `["e", <dm-id>]`, but the DM id itself is only known after unwrap of the original message — we need a join on already-unwrapped events client-side.
- [ ] Storage: extend the existing DM tables (`outgoing_dms`, conversation cache) with a reactions side-table keyed by `(conversation_id, message_id, reactor_pubkey)`, or denormalize onto the message row.
- [ ] Send reliability: reactions should ride the same retry / self-wrap recovery path as DMs (see #4106, #4241, #4410) — a half-delivered reaction is worse than no reaction.
- [ ] Notifications: react-to-DM notifications would themselves need to be encrypted, which is a deeper decision. Out of scope for v1 — start with in-app only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Long-pressing a DM bubble surfaces a reactions row above the existing actions sheet.
- [ ] Tapping a reaction publishes a wrapped reaction event to both self and recipient and optimistically renders the chip.
- [ ] Tapping the same reaction again removes it (publishes a NIP-09 deletion of the reaction).
- [ ] Reaction chip renders under the message bubble with emoji + count; own reaction is visually distinct.
- [ ] Reactions persist across app restarts (stored locally, not re-fetched on every cold start).
- [ ] Reactions survive the same failure modes DMs do: self-wrap-only recovery, recipient-failed sweeps, etc.
- [ ] Reactions are NOT discoverable on public relays as "X reacted to a DM" — only the involved pubkeys can decrypt.
- [ ] Works for both NIP-17 DMs and the legacy NIP-04 path if both are still live in production at ship time.

## Notes

- Related: #4620 (DM multi-line input), #4621 (DM markdown formatting — merged via #4631). This sits alongside those as the next DM UX gap.
- Prior art in this repo: existing NIP-25 plumbing in `mobile/packages/likes_repository/`, NIP-17 send/receive flow in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/`, retry infrastructure in `mobile/lib/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service.dart`. Reuse the retry primitive, do NOT reuse `likes_repository` unmodified — the privacy envelope is the whole point.
- A short design doc / brainstorm under `mobile/docs/brainstorm/` should land before implementation kicks off, given the spec questions above.

title: feat(observability): enrich Bloc error reports with last event, state, and build tag (#3758)
body:
## Description

`DivineBlocObserver` now enriches the Crashlytics reports it forwards with the bloc's most recent **event**, **state**, and **transition time** — closing the per-error triage gap raised as concern #3 in PR #3534's review (the same gap that made the #3503 auth-timing investigation expensive).

- Tracks the latest event per bloc via `onEvent` and the latest state via `onChange`, stored in a per-bloc `Expando` (keys held weakly → observing every bloc retains nothing; **no IO until `onError`**).
- On a forwarded `ReportableError`, attaches `bloc.lastEvent` / `bloc.lastState` / `bloc.lastTransitionAt` as Crashlytics custom keys — each run through `sanitizeForCrashReport` (npub/nsec/email stripped) — **before** `recordError`, so they attach to the report it emits.
- `main.dart` sets a `build_tag` custom key (`"${version}+${buildNumber}"`) once at startup, so per-error triage no longer needs to cross-reference the release dashboard.

Dispatch is fire-and-forget but **synchronous and in order**, so the platform-channel messages stay ordered without blocking the bloc error path. (First cut routed `recordError` through an `await`ed helper, which deferred it past a microtask and broke the suite's synchronous-dispatch contract — restructured to preserve both that contract and the keys-before-recordError ordering.)

**Related Issue:** Closes #3758 (part of epic #4336)

## Out of Scope

- The per-feature `addError` Reportable migration sweeps — already shipped under #4336.
- #3415 (upload-timeout fatal misclassification) — coordinates with this PR's `recordError` path but ships separately.

- `flutter test test/observability/` → **27/27 pass** (9 observer tests, incl. 3 new: key-ordering via `verifyInOrder`, no-keys-when-nothing-observed, state-snapshot PII sanitization)

title: observability: enrich Crashlytics context for Bloc errors (event name / state snapshot / build tag)
body:
Follow-up from PR #3534's review — addresses concern #3 in @hm21's original blocker list, which was deferred from PR1 with an explicit follow-up offer.

## Current state (after PR #3534)

`DivineBlocObserver` forwards to Crashlytics:
- `error.runtimeType` (used as the dashboard grouping key)
- the stack trace
- the sanitized inner-error `toString()` (npub/nsec stripped)
- the observer's `reason` annotation: `Bloc.addError <BlocType>`
- the optional `Reportable.context` call-site tag

## Gap

When triaging a Crashlytics report, you can see *which bloc* raised, but not:
- which **event** was in flight when the error fired (handler-throw or `addError` from inside a handler)
- the **state snapshot** at the time of the error
- the **build tag** / app version (Crashlytics has this generally, but cross-referencing per-error is friction)

For race conditions like #3503 — where the symptom depends on auth-state timing — that triage gap is what made the original investigation expensive.

## Proposed surface

- Track the latest event per bloc via `BlocObserver.onEvent` (or `onTransition`) → store as a per-bloc field on the observer.
- Track the latest state per bloc via `BlocObserver.onChange` → same.
- On `onError`, set Crashlytics custom keys (`bloc.lastEvent`, `bloc.lastState`, `bloc.lastTransitionAt`) before `recordError`.
- Sanitize state snapshots through `sanitizeForCrashReport()` before they leave the device — same npub/nsec handling.
- Build tag: surface via `FirebaseCrashlytics.setCustomKey('build_tag', ...)` once at startup, not per-error.

## Out of scope

- The per-feature `addError` migration stack (PR2–PR7). That is purely the call-site classification work; this issue is a separate observability-layer change.
- Replacing the existing `Log.error` + `addError` pair convention.

## References

- PR #3534 — establishes the observer + matrix
- Discussion: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3534#discussion_r3169300470 (open inline thread on `Reportable.context`, where the typed-id direction was deferred for the same reasons that apply here)

## Description

Add web support to the `divine_video_player` package via a new `HtmlVideoElementBackend` that drives a browser `HTMLVideoElement` using `dart:js_interop` and `package:web`.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4464

## What Changed

### New: `HtmlVideoElementBackend` (web)

- Full `WebVideoPlayerBackend` implementation using `HTMLVideoElement` via `dart:ui_web` / `package:web`
- Clip-range playback: `setClip()` enforces `clip.start` (seek on load) and `clip.end` (soft clamp via `timeupdate` listener)
- Autoplay-safe volume: `setVolume(0)` also sets `muted = true` so browsers honour the autoplay policy; raised again later if volume increases
- Platform-view lookup is handled through a static `_elementRegistry` keyed by `viewType`; registry entries are removed on `dispose()`, while the platform-view factory remains registered for the browser session because `platformViewRegistry` has no unregister API

- `DivineVideoPlayerWebPlugin` registers the platform view factory via `dart:ui_web`

Two `@visibleForTesting` static hooks make the web backend testable without a real browser:

| Hook | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `debugForceWebBackend` | Forces web backend selection — necessary because `kIsWeb` is always `false` in the Dart VM |
| `webBackendFactory` | Injects a fake `WebVideoPlayerBackend` — necessary because `HtmlVideoElementBackend` requires a live `HTMLVideoElement` in the browser DOM |

Without **both** hooks, the controller's web code path is completely unreachable from unit tests.

title: fix(video): recover collaborator invites from outgoing dm queue
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4636 by making collaborator invite recovery queue-backed and durable instead of relying on a one-shot snackbar retry after publish.

Before this change, a successful video publish could still leave collaborator invites unsent. Those failures were surfaced only through a short-lived snackbar, and the manual retry path minted a brand new invite DM instead of recovering the original queued send. That meant users could easily miss the retry affordance, and any future persistent retry UI would risk duplicate invites if the original queued DM later recovered.

This PR changes the recovery model to use the existing `outgoing_dms` queue as the single source of truth.

## Root Cause

The issue was not that collaborator invites had no persistence. They were already enqueued in `outgoing_dms` before publish. The real gaps were:

- successful video publish treated collaborator invite delivery as best-effort
- failure feedback was ephemeral and easy to miss
- manual retry re-sent a fresh collaborator invite instead of recovering the queued rumor
- diagnostics were not specific enough to distinguish video publish failures from collaborator invite delivery failures

## What Changed

### Queue-backed collaborator invite recovery

- Added `CollaboratorInviteRecoveryService` to parse collaborator invite rows from `outgoing_dms`
- Grouped unresolved invites by video address for author-facing recovery
- Retried by calling `DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId: ...)` on the original queued row
- Filtered the persistent banner to recipient-delivery failures so self-wrap-only recovery does not create false author-facing alarms

### Persistent author-side recovery UI

- Added Riverpod providers to expose the recovery service and pending invite groups
- Added a persistent inline banner on the author's own profile video grid for videos with unresolved collaborator invite delivery
- Wired banner retry to queue recovery instead of creating a new invite message
- Updated the publish snackbar retry button to use the same queue-backed recovery path

### Diagnostics and cleanup

- Enriched collaborator invite failure logging in `VideoPublishService` with video address, creator pubkey, and per-invite failure details
- Enriched NIP-17 send failure logging with rumor id and recipient pubkey
- Enriched video event publish logging with configured and connected relay counts plus failure reason when available
- Removed the old duplicate-prone `retryCollaboratorInvite()` resend path so there is one retry mechanism instead of two

## Why This Is Safer

- The retry path now recovers the original queued send instead of minting a second collaborator invite rumor
- The UI is driven from durable queue state, so it survives navigation and app restarts
- Auto-retry and manual retry now operate on the same underlying queue record rather than competing mechanisms
- The author-facing banner only appears for unresolved recipient delivery, which is the user-visible failure mode

## Tests

title: fix(firebase): use real Android config and gate unsupported platforms (#3343)
body:
## Description

`DefaultFirebaseOptions.android` was a placeholder (`openvine-placeholder`) even though `android/app/google-services.json` points at the real `openvine-co` project. Because `CrashReportingService.initialize()` passes `DefaultFirebaseOptions.currentPlatform`, **Android initialised Firebase/Crashlytics against a bogus project and its crash signal was silently lost** — the high-severity core of #3343.

**Step 2 of #3343** (Step 1 = docs/comment in #4667). Implements the agreed platform decision: **iOS + macOS + Android supported; web/windows off.**

- **Android → real config**, hand-derived from the committed `google-services.json` (no Firebase-console access needed): appId `1:972941478875:android:c716006682f92d9444b5fe`, project `openvine-co`, etc.
- **`firebase.json`** gains the `android` platform + dart configuration entry.
- **web/windows removed**: `currentPlatform` throws `UnsupportedError` for them, and `isFirebaseSupported` excludes web. For every non-web platform the new gate is **mathematically identical** to the old (`!kIsWeb && A && B` ≡ `kIsWeb || (A && B)` when `kIsWeb` is `false`), so the only runtime change is web.
- **New `firebase_options_test.dart`**: asserts android/iOS/macOS resolve to `openvine-co` with non-placeholder keys; `currentPlatform` returns real config on supported platforms and throws on windows/linux/fuchsia.

> ⚠️ **Web FCM implication (please sanity-check):** excluding web from `isFirebaseSupported` also disables Firebase Messaging on web (`pushNotificationServiceProvider` returns `null`). This **never worked** — web Firebase config was a placeholder — so this formalises reality rather than removing a working feature. If web push is on the roadmap it needs real web Firebase config first (separate work).

**Related Issue:** Relates to #3343

## Out of Scope

- **Step 3 (CI/DevOps):** apply the Android `com.google.firebase.crashlytics` Gradle plugin + add a mapping-file upload to `codemagic.yaml` so Android release crashes symbolicate (acceptance criterion 4 for Android). Recommend a DevOps follow-up; **#3343 stays open** until then (hence `Relates to`, not `Closes`).
- **Header comment** in `firebase_options.dart` (lines 1–2) — owned by #4667, intentionally untouched here to avoid an overlapping diff.
- **macOS appId** reuses the iOS appId (no macOS-specific source in-repo) — flagged inline for `flutterfire configure` confirmation.

## Verification

- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` (4 .dart files) → clean
- `flutter analyze` (changed files) → No issues found
- `firebase.json` validates as JSON
- `flutter test test/firebase_options_test.dart test/utils/platform_support_test.dart` → **14/14 pass** (4 new + 10 existing)
- No other test references the old config

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

title: fix(security): remove BYOK nsec from Keycast OAuth PKCE verifier and request body
body:
Source audit context: fresh `origin/main` worktree `.worktrees/audit-codebase-2026-04-24` at commit `33f6e026a`.
This issue was generated from the April 2026 codebase audit and includes file/line evidence from that snapshot.

## Severity
Critical

## Problem
BYOK registration embeds the user nsec into the PKCE verifier and posts the nsec to Keycast during headless registration.

## Evidence
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/pkce.dart:9-12 appends .$nsec to the PKCE verifier.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:155-171 accepts optional nsec and uses it in verifier generation.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:280-286 derives BYOK pubkey and generates verifier with nsec.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:299-301 puts nsec into the registration request body.
- mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart:81-95 exports local nsec and passes it into registration.
- mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart:117-122 calls headlessRegister(... nsec: nsec ...).

## Impact
BYOK/private key material leaves local storage and is also carried in the PKCE verifier, breaking the expected local-key custody boundary.

## Recommended fix
Never send or embed nsec. Use a local proof-of-possession challenge signed by the key, or send only byok_pubkey and a signature over server-provided nonce/session data.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No nsec appears in OAuth URL, PKCE verifier, persisted pending verification, request body, logs, or tests.
- [ ] Server receives only public key plus proof.
- [ ] BYOK registration still binds the account to the intended Nostr pubkey.
- [ ] Tests assert verifier does not contain nsec1.

## Related issues
Adjacent: #969, #3066, #3270.
